becomeascout.title: Become a member
becomeascout.subtitle: OF OUR ADVENTURE GROUP OF FRIENDS
becomeascout.description: In Scouterna you will find both challenges and new friends, no matter where you live or how old you are. Here you can experience adventures in nature, discover new ways to solve problems or just have fun together while we explore the world. And of course you are involved in deciding what we will come up with.

becomealeader.title: Become a leader
becomealeader.subtitle: IN SCOUTING TROUPE WITH POWER
becomealeader.description: As an adult, there are excellent opportunities to develop as a leader with us. You don't have to be an experienced sailor to participate in our activities. You don't have to be an old scout to become a leader either. The only requirement is that you have a genuine interest in working with young people and that you are interested in working voluntarily in a well-functioning scout corps. The corps pays for the training you need to function well as a scout leader.

aboutus.title: About us
aboutus.descriptionOne: Hässelby Strands Sjöscoutkår (HSS) is a traditional non-profit youth organization with a focus on scouting and boating. We are religiously and politically independent, and a member of the Swedish Scout Association, which with approximately 65,000 members is one of Sweden's largest youth organizations.
aboutus.descriptionTwo: The goal of our activities is to give children and young people the opportunity to experience nature, boating, seamanship, challenges and - above all - camaraderie. The basic idea is Learning by doing. There is no substitute bench in the scouts!
aboutus.descriptionThree: The Scout Corps was formed in 1959 and operates in a pleasant premises (called Ruffen) on the shores of Lake Mälaren in Hässelby. The Corps has around 130 happy members, owns five sailboats, ten optimist dinghies, two 2-krona boats, a fast escort boat and a large scout cabin.

sjohumlor.title: Sjöhumlor -
sjohumlor.subtitle: Spårare 8-9 years
sjohumlor.description: At the age of 8 you can start in HSS, i.e. when you start in grade 2. You then become a Scout Scout and a member of the Sjöhumlorna department. (Previously Scout Scout was called "mini scout") We have meetings every week and overnight stays, both hikes and longer camps
sjohumlor.fullDescription:
You can start at HSS at the age of 8, that is, when you begin school year 2. You then become a Tracker Scout and a member of the Sjöhumlorna ('Sea Bumblebees') section. (Tracker Scout was previously called 'Minior Scout'.)
We have meetings every week as well as overnight stays, both hikes and longer camps. Here the children get to learn knots, basic nature knowledge and seamanship in a playful way.
You learn something new almost every day in the Scouts. It's always fun things, but sometimes they're also really useful to know — like whittling with a knife or putting a bandage on someone who's hurt themselves. Unlike how it's done in school, we don't read any books about knives and bandages; we learn by doing, by trying everything out for real instead. While we do it, we work together in patrols, small groups where everyone gets a say. That's clever, because together you can always help each other come up with even more fun things to do.
We sail Optimist dinghies and 2-Crowns (tvåkronor).
Sjöhumlorna meet on Mondays in our lovely premises, Ruffen, by Hässelby Strandbad.
When you're a scout you always do your best, and it doesn't matter if something happens to go wrong — that's why we usually reflect a little on how everything went, so that we get better for next time.

kaparna.title: Karpana -
kaparna.subtitle: Upptäckare 10-11 years
kaparna.description: At Kaparna, you start at the age of 10 and stay for two years until it's time for the next step. (Previously, scout scouts were called "junior scouts") At Kaparna, the difficulty of the tasks increases.
kaparna.fullDescription:
At Kaparna you start at the age of 10 and stay for two years until it's time for the next step. (Discoverer Scout was previously called 'Junior Scout'.) At Kaparna the difficulty of the tasks increases.
The scouts get to learn to sail an Optimist as well as try sailing a 2-Crown (tvåkrona) and a keelboat.
A fully trained Discoverer Scout can, among other things, handle a knife, light fires and put out small fires, sail an Optimist on their own, as well as basic first aid and water safety.
The Kaparna section meets on Tuesdays in our premises, Ruffen, by Hässelby Strandbad.
When you're a scout you always do your best, but it doesn't matter if something happens to go wrong — that's why we usually reflect a little on how everything went, so that we get better for next time.

konvojen.title: Konvojen -
konvojen.subtitle: Äventyrare 12-14 years
konvojen.description: At the age of 12, the doors to the Adventure Scouts open. For three exciting years, you get to learn useful things in seamanship and nature. (Previously, Adventure Scouts were called "Patrol Scouts")
konvojen.fullDescription:
At the age of 12 the doors to the Adventurer Scouts open. For three exciting years you get to learn useful things within seamanship and nature. (Adventurer Scout was previously called 'Patrol Scout'.)
This is where the sailing begins in earnest, and it takes us out into the archipelago in the summer. When we're not sailing we practise navigation and also do traditional land scouting activities.
In winter, when it's at its coldest, we have a proper winter hike where we live in tents. Another highlight is the traditional ice-hole dip that no Patrol Scout gets out of…
Konvojen meets on Thursdays.

utmanare.title: Utmanare -
utmanare.subtitle: 15+ years
utmanare.description: HSS challenger scout team never ceases to exist! After your time as challenger scout, you are a close-knit group. It is not unusual for you to stay in touch for life. (Previously, this department was called "senior scout")
utmanare.fullDescription:
An HSS Challenger Scout team never ceases to exist! After the time as a Challenger Scout you're a tightly knit bunch. It's not uncommon to stay in touch for life. (This section was previously called 'Senior Scout'.)
When you come up from the Adventurer Scouts you form a team together with your year group. Then you work towards learning new things and taking on harder challenges to strengthen the team spirit.
During the first years you have leaders with you, and as you develop you become a leader yourself on the other sections.
The Challenger Scouts sail on their own in the archipelago once they've reached a sufficient level of knowledge.
Each Challenger Scout team comes up with its own name (by tradition they end in -arne, and the team is called 'fjantarne' until they've come up with a name of their own).
Meetings take place on Tuesdays or Wednesdays.

familjescouting.title: Familjescouting
familjescouting.description: Through Family Scouting, children under the age of eight, together with one or more adults, get to encounter scouting in a fun and playful way. Family Scouting is also an excellent way to bring more adults into the troop.
familjescouting.fullDescription:
Family Scouting is for children under the age of eight and an adult the child feels safe with. Together you discover scouting through play, adventure and fun activities.
Children and adults take part side by side and help each other with the activities. The adult is responsible for the child, but is also an important part of the community and takes part just as much as the children.
The adult can be a parent, grandparent, relative or another close person.
The focus in Family Scouting is for children and adults to experience things together and strengthen their relationship.

boatHistory.title: OUR BOAT HISTORY
boatHistory.description: Founded in 1959, the Scout troop operates from a welcoming clubhouse known as Ruffen, located on the shores of Lake Mälaren in Hässelby. The troop has around 130 active members and owns five sailboats, ten Optimist dinghies, two Two Kronor sailboats, a fast support boat, and a large scout cabin.

buildingMyset.title: BUILDING MYSET
buildingMyset.description: Myset is our cabin in Lövsta. On Sunday, January 28, 1968, Myset was officially inaugurated. By that time, HSS's Parents Association had spent three years building and developing the cabin. The project cost nearly SEK 50,000, funds that were raised through bazaars and lotteries. Nearly 400 eager scouts and parents attended the inauguration ceremony. They witnessed the formal handover of the key from the Chair of the Parents Association, Agne Stavegren, to the Chair of HSS, Lennart Carlbom.
buildingMyset.descriptionTwo: Here we have managed to find a few photos from a bygone era.
